answer:
**Answer: 19,159 sites (sample-site rows) are removed** when filtering Zebra Finch sites that do not show >90% or <10% methylation (i.e., rows with methylation in the closed band [10%, 90%] are removed; boundary values at exactly 90% or exactly 10% are removed per the strict ">90% or <10%" wording).

Executed results from the reproducible script `analysis_zf_methylation_filter.py`:
- ZF input: 19,698 sample-site rows, 1,140 unique genomic sites (Pos), MethylationPercentage on a 0–100 percent scale (min 0.0, max 100.0).
- Rows kept (>90% or <10%): 539 — comprising 268 rows >90% and 271 rows <10%.
- **Rows removed (10% ≤ methylation ≤ 90%): 19,159** ← primary answer.
- Boundary handling: 13 rows at exactly 90% and 8 rows at exactly 10% are counted as removed (strict wording); a strictly exclusive band (10% < M < 90%) would remove 19,138 rows instead — a 21-row difference.
- Sensitivity note (unique-site/Pos variants, transparency only, as requested): (a) if a site is kept whenever ANY of its sample rows shows >90% or <10% methylation (removed only when every sample row of the site falls in the 10–90% band), **849 of 1,140 unique sites are removed** (291 kept); (b) if a site's aggregate methylation (mean/median/pooled methylated counts) is used, all 1,140 sites fall in the band → 1,140 removed, 0 kept (degenerate, confirming the row-level reading is the sensible one).
- Per the approved scope, the JD data and chromosome-length files were not used.
